dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: You mean the "mortal paradise" that I do not even dare imagine in my post-hoc recollections...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: From Hyperborea in the north to Lang-Gan in the south, Delphi, and this place, what used to be Arcadia...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: What do you want to know? What we ate, what we thought, or what we made?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: It's not that I do not wish to tell you everything, one by one. It's just that once you hear me out, you'll probably think us merely children of some intellect.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: We ate the same things you do. We were able to think about matters far removed from reality only because the priests and angels always gave us the answers to the practical issues.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: We created playthings, mere trifles, that amused us, because nothing we made would match the exalted means the heavens had already bestowed upon us.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: It's like we were children doing something that pleased our parents.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: A fellow named Bosch drew a piece called "The Mortal Paradise" based on what I told him. He captured the feeling exactly — the very feeling.
